description: Open source repositories that are in scope for active bug bounty programs, ordered by newest stable release first.

repos.name: googleapis/google-cloud-ruby
repos.description: Apache-2.0 licensed monorepo of idiomatic Ruby client library gems for Google Cloud APIs, well over 200 of them, the large majority generated by the GAPIC generator and each versioned, tagged and released separately so the repository publishes new gem releases most days. In scope for the Google Open Source Software VRP on bughunters.google.com, whose scope rule covers all up-to-date versions of open source software stored in the public repositories of Google-owned GitHub organizations, naming google, googleapis and GoogleCloudPlatform explicitly. The rules revised on 2026-03-19 sort covered repositories into OT0 (Flagship), OT1 (Important), OT2 (Standard) and OT3 (Low-Priority); Google's published OT0/OT1 manifest (google/bughunters, oss-repository-tier/external_repositories.txtpb, 78 entries) contains no googleapis repository, so this one sits in OT2, described as active, stable projects often published in major package managers. That tier placement is the material caveat: for OT2 and OT3 Google no longer pays money or gives credit for Product Vulnerabilities or Other Security Issues, and only Supply Chain Compromises are still rewarded, with the OT2 maximum lowered to $3,133.70. Latest stable release: google-cloud-sql-v1/v0.3.0 (2026-08-06, 22:00 UTC), one of roughly a dozen gem releases published that evening and not a pre-release.

repos.name: Azure/azure-sdk-for-java
repos.description: MIT licensed monorepo holding active development of the Azure SDK for Java, both the client libraries used to consume Azure services and the azure-resourcemanager management libraries, built over a shared HTTP pipeline that supplies retries, logging, tracing and authentication; each artifact is versioned and published to Maven Central on its own cadence, with several releases landing on a typical day. In scope for the Microsoft Open Source Bounty Program run by MSRC, which enumerates its targets as Azure SDKs limited to azure/azure-sdk, azure/azure-sdk-for-net, azure/azure-sdk-for-python, azure/azure-sdk-for-js, azure/azure-sdk-for-java, azure/azure-sdk-for-go, azure/azure-sdk-for-rust and azure/azure-sdk-tools, alongside FluentUI, PowerShell 7, TypeScript, Visual Studio Code, Microsoft Agent Framework, Monaco-editor and MsQuic. Awards run $750 to $15,000 USD and the program requires that the vulnerability be Critical or Important severity and reproducible on the most recent actively maintained branch, so findings confined to an older servicing branch do not pay; the policy was last revised 2026-06-22. This repository's coverage comes solely from that program, because the separate Microsoft Azure bounty explicitly puts vulnerabilities in open-source components, libraries or repositories and vulnerabilities in SDKs out of scope. Latest stable release: com.azure+azure-ai-agents_2.3.0 (2026-08-06, 21:55 UTC); same-day 1.0.0-beta.1 preview tags in this repository are badged pre-release by GitHub and were excluded.

repos.name: googleapis/google-cloud-node
repos.description: Apache-2.0 licensed monorepo of idiomatic Node.js client libraries for Google Cloud Platform services, well over 100 individually versioned packages authored in TypeScript and published to npm, with release-please cutting tagged GitHub releases in batches several times a week. In scope for the Google Open Source Software VRP on bughunters.google.com under the same org-wide rule that covers every public repository in Google-owned GitHub organizations, googleapis included, and repository configuration such as GitHub Actions workflows and access control is covered as well as library code. Like the Ruby monorepo it is absent from Google's OT0/OT1 tier manifest, so it falls in the OT2 Standard tier created by the 2026-03-19 rules revision, where Supply Chain Compromises are the only rewarded category and are capped at $3,133.70, while Product Vulnerabilities and Other Security Issues in OT2 and OT3 repositories now earn neither payment nor credit. Latest stable release: databasecenter/v0.4.1 (2026-08-06, 21:46 UTC), badged Latest by GitHub and published together with bigtable v7.1.0, bigquery v9.0.1, gcp-metadata v9.0.1, googleapis-common v9.0.1 and pack-n-play v5.0.1 in the same release-please batch.
